title: Rome, January 1478 st. fior. (1479): Giovanni Mazzinghi and an unsigned writer to the Medici, word-by-word cipher (ASF MAP LXXXIX 142, CXXXVII 252; key source MAP LXXII 170)

documents.shelfmark: ASF, Mediceo avanti il Principato LXXXIX 142
documents.date: 16 January 1478 st. fior. ("In nome di Dio a dì xvj di gennaio 1478"; place not stated, Rome by content)

plaintext.source: Bare: no decipherment on or beside the leaf (vetting batch n08).

documents.shelfmark: ASF, Mediceo avanti il Principato CXXXVII 252
documents.route: unsigned (same hand and signs as 2307) -> the Medici

system.summary: Homophonic letter substitution in letter-like signs, word by word with word division kept, clear words interspersed, numerals as code words for persons.
system.sibling_key: MAP LXXII 170, same signs, with a contemporary interlinear decipherment

prior_solution.where: No decipherment of 2307 or 2320 found; the sibling LXXII 170 carries its own contemporary gloss.

conditions.human_role: Daniel Bourdeau chose the target; the model does the work. A second session worked 2307 from the catalogue task prompt (ciphertext only) at the same time; no target-specific intervention.

solution.what: Full-size images of MAP LXXXIX 142, CXXXVII 252, LXXII 170 and neighbours downloaded from the ASF MAP viewer (getdoc.py).
Datelines read: all three 'gennaio 1478', i.e. January 1479 modern (Florentine style); 2307 headed 'In Roma'; LXXII 170 verso is show-through only.

Glyph inventory (glyphs.md, 45 tokens) and transcription of the glossed sibling MAP LXXII 170 with its interlinear decipherment (t170.tsv: 194 cipher words, 154 with a gloss, 73 of them h/m confidence); glosses drift left of their words and were assigned by word order.

Key fitted on 69 confident cipher-word/gloss pairs of LXXII 170 by hard-EM monotone alignment (build_key.py, key.tsv): homophonic letter substitution with word division kept, e.g. + a, x/y e, s/5/1/3 i, r o, n n, H t, 6 r, o d, q u, {sg} c, 2+ l, p p, 4 s, 8 m, m g, = b; numerals are code words for persons. Held-out fifth over four splits: 57-74% of letters, limited by the glosses' legibility and alignment.

Sign-by-sign transcription of the two bare letters with the 170 token set plus new tokens (glyphs.md 'New in 252/142'): MAP CXXXVII 252 (t252.tsv: 14 lines, 121 cipher words, 595 signs, 7 clear words, 4 numerals) and MAP LXXXIX 142 (t142.tsv: 37 lines, 209 cipher words, 1109 signs, 132 clear words, 13 numerals). New tokens {dbar} {3bar} {eq3} {Hp} {B} {h} {pbar} {T} {nn} {phi} {/o/}; {Hp} is the form 170 transcribed # in 'letere'. No decipherment or gloss on either letter. The 142 dateline reads '+ In nom[e] d[i] d[io] a dì xvj di gennaio 1478', not 'In Roma'.
Bare letters transcribed with the same tokens: t252.tsv (121 cipher words, 595 signs) and t142.tsv (209 cipher words, 1,109 signs); new signs {Hp}, {dbar}, {pbar}, {T} and others added to glyphs.md.

Signs absent from the glossed pairs given values by it-cinquecento 5-gram hill-climbing over both letters (refine.py), then fixed by word context where the LM chose badly: {pbar}/{dbar} p, {Hp} tt, b f, g ss, c e (key_refined.tsv).

Draft decryption of both bare letters (draft252.txt, draft142.txt) reads as Italian through most words: 252 on a papal brief and fear that Antonio del Palagio, Pagolo Rucellai and Lionardo di Giunta will be seized; 142 (Mazzinghi) on a bull annulling privileges, a cruel process against the Medici, and Iacopo de' Rossi da Pistoia and a Pistoiese called Cola, with 'ordinò la morte di [30]'. Look-alike signs (o/q, #/h, t) still misread in places.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: First pass of 89/142, 29 sign classes, 1055 signs.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Paired the 72/170 gloss with its cipher; only 'publichamente mostra lectere' aligned with confidence.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Homophonic annealer on it-cinquecento; collapsed onto all-i.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Same with a letter-frequency KL penalty and swap moves; Italian came out (contra di voi molto crudele, molte volte, grandissimo).
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: 537-sign Italian passage in a random 29-sign homophonic key: 655/667 letters right.
Parallel session (PR #301), 2307 without the sibling key: Second transcription pass in 3x crops and word-by-word reading; merged sign classes resolved from context.
